name: the-favourites-hold-their-places-through-the-overview
description:
The Overview close narrows the sidebar from 380 to the user's width over 150ms, laid out at the live width on every tick. The favourites grid is auto-fill, so a rest width of 160-213 shows the tiles jump 4 columns -> 3 -> 2 as the slot narrows, reordering every tile after the second. The fix caps the grid to the settled rest width for the length of the crossing (--atrium-rest-width, set from the Overview open until the close has narrowed), so it holds one column count throughout instead of re-flowing on every tick.

THE FIXTURE stages sidebarWidth 160 with sidebarWidthMigrated true and 6 favourites under profile Default - a rest width of 214 or more shows 4 columns at both ends of the crossing and cannot fail.

THE GATES are copied from overview-widens-the-sidebar.json: dx=+90 at (140,300) reaches the Overview pane, dx=-90 mirrors it back. After the rail parks on the Overview, a sampler is armed in /sidebar: a ResizeObserver on document.documentElement plus a capped rAF loop (rAF alone is starved during the resize), each tick recording the live sidebar width, the grid's computed column count, and every tile's offsetTop:offsetLeft. The close swipe runs under scroll_during_capture so the frames are on hand for a manual crop-level check alongside the numeric one.

saw-narrow GATES the two checks below it: without at least one sample at 160 < w < 380, a run that never saw the narrow width could pass the column/position checks vacuously. cols-held asks whether the grid ever showed more than one distinct column count (it must not, the whole crossing must read as one column count). positions-held asks the same of each tile's own offset, which is what a column-count change actually looks like on screen. Both answer the actual set on failure rather than a plain false.

actions.expression: (() => { window.__fav = []; const g = document.querySelector('#atrium-root > .favgrid'); if (!g) { return 'no-grid'; } const s = () => window.__fav.push({w: document.documentElement.clientWidth, cols: getComputedStyle(g).gridTemplateColumns.split(' ').length, pos: [...g.querySelectorAll('.fav')].map(t => t.offsetTop + ':' + t.offsetLeft).join(',')}); window.__favObs = new ResizeObserver(s); window.__favObs.observe(document.documentElement); const tick = () => { s(); if (window.__fav.length < 200) { window.__favRaf = requestAnimationFrame(tick); } }; tick(); return 'armed'; })()
actions.note: armed on the Overview pane, before the close swipe, so no tick of the narrow is missed. ResizeObserver plus a capped rAF loop: rAF alone is starved during the resize (sidebar.js onRailPaint)
the same gesture mirrored, back onto the first workspace - this is the narrow the sampler has to catch. Kept as a capture for a frame-level crop check alongside the numeric one
the close settles the pane, then the width animation runs for 150ms

actions.expression: (() => { const hit = window.__fav.some((r) => r.w > 160 && r.w < 380); return hit ? 'saw-narrow' : 'no-narrow, widths=' + JSON.stringify([...new Set(window.__fav.map((r) => r.w))]); })()
actions.note: GATES the two checks below: without a sample strictly between 160 and 380, a run that never saw the narrow could pass them vacuously

actions.expression: (() => { const cols = new Set(window.__fav.map((r) => r.cols)); return (cols.size === 1 && cols.has(2)) ? 'cols-held' : 'cols=' + JSON.stringify([...cols]); })()
actions.note: AC: one column count for the whole crossing, not 4 -> 3 -> 2. Answers the actual set on failure

actions.expression: (() => { const pos = new Set(window.__fav.map((r) => r.pos)); return pos.size === 1 ? 'positions-held' : 'positions=' + JSON.stringify([...pos]); })()
actions.note: AC: no tile ever moves to a different slot mid-crossing. Answers the actual set on failure
the user's own width came back once the crossing settled
